pithy

/PITH-ee/ - rhymes with smithy · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Pithy means brief while packed with meaning.

Grandpa's fishing advice was pithy: 'Early, quiet, patient — pick all three.'

Example

The med-school dean ends orientation with one pithy sentence — 'Listen; the patient is telling you the diagnosis' — and steps away from the podium. Students spend four years unpacking how much instruction those eight words carry.

Pithy praises compression with content: brief and packed with meaning, both at once. Short alone does not earn the word — 'No comment' is brief and empty — and a pithy line, unlike a gnomic one, stays perfectly clear while it compresses.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

punchy: Punchy praises impact — a line that lands hard and fast, though it may carry nothing once the jolt fades. Pithy demands more: the line must be brief and packed with meaning, so the freight survives the compression. A slogan can be punchy and hollow; a pithy sentence keeps unpacking for years.

compact: Compact says something is tightly packed for its size, and it works for wording and objects alike — a compact car, a compact paragraph. Pithy is reserved for language, and it certifies the cargo too: brief and packed with meaning, not merely small. Compact measures the packing; pithy vouches for what is packed.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

long-winded: using many words where few would serve

rambling: wandering from point to point without arriving

Where it sits · how densely the meaning is compressed

brief → pithy → gnomic

brief vs. pithy: Brief is a smaller compliment than pithy — brief only promises the thing is short, not that the meaning survived the cut.

gnomic vs. pithy: Gnomic goes further than pithy: compressed past clarity, so the reader must puzzle out what a pithy line would have made plain.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — pith: the soft core of a plant stem (Old English pitha)

Suffix — -y: adjective: full of

Put it together: Pith + -y = full of pith. Pith is the nutrient core at a stem's center — so a pithy saying is all core: peel away nothing, because nothing is peel.

Use the root in a new word: pith: She peeled every last scrap of pith off the orange before juicing it.

Word Choice

neutral / admiring

Pithy is a compliment with teeth: it certifies both brevity and freight. If a line is merely short, say brief; if it is short and unsoftened, blunt may fit better; keep pithy for the sentence that folds a paragraph's worth of meaning into a breath.
